title: Role of the Drive in Mediating Correlations Between Two Qubits Through a Shared Dissipative Cavity
authors: Nozhat Ghaseminezhad, Vahid Ameri, Alidad Askari
abstract: Using a numerically exact master equation, we demonstrate that two qubits, coupled solely through a shared damped, driven cavity, can become correlated. The drive influences both the amount and the type of correlation. For parametric, coherent, and resonantly modulated drives, the qubits develop quantum discord that increases with cavity temperature, while the logarithmic negativity remains numerically zero. This indicates the presence of discord without entanglement. In contrast, a time-modulated parametric drive is the only one that generates genuine two-qubit entanglement, achieving \(E_\mathcal{N} \simeq 0.15\) and concurrence \(\simeq 0.16\) at \((\eps, γ) = (0.3, 0.2)\), which rises to \(E_\mathcal{N} \simeq 0.32\) in the weak-coupling, moderate-damping region. Heating eventually destroys this entanglement around \(n_{\mathrm{th}} \simeq 0.2\), while discord continues to grow, resulting in a temperature-driven transition from entanglement to discord within a single drive. Moreover, the parametric drive offers the best protection for single-qubit coherence, unlike the coherent and modulated drives. An adiabatic-elimination model indicates that the cavity generates an effective coupling and a collective dephasing channel, both of which increase with temperature, explaining the observed discord without entanglement.
summary: This paper investigates how driving a shared dissipative cavity mediates correlations between two qubits. It finds that while static drives only generate quantum discord, a time-modulated parametric drive can generate genuine entanglement at low temperatures. Crucially, increasing thermal noise causes the system to undergo a transition from entanglement to a state characterized only by discord.
main_problem: To determine how the specific driving mechanism applied to a shared dissipative cavity controls the nature and magnitude of quantum correlations (discord vs. entanglement) between two coupled qubits.
main_result: The time-modulated parametric drive is uniquely capable of generating genuine two-qubit entanglement at low temperatures, which subsequently decays into a state exhibiting only quantum discord as temperature increases.
method: The study employs numerical simulation of the master equation, often utilizing an adiabatic elimination technique to derive an effective two-qubit model.
model_or_system: The system consists of two qubits coupled solely through a single, shared, damped, and driven optical cavity mode. The dynamics are governed by the master equation incorporating dissipation and various driving Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Quantum Discord, Entanglement (Logarithmic Negativity, Concurrence), and single-qubit coherence ($\ell_1$-norm).
important_parameters: Cavity temperature ($n_{	ext{th}}$), coupling strength ($\epsilon$), and damping rate ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the adiabatic elimination of the cavity mode to derive an effective two-qubit Hamiltonian and dissipation channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the growth of quantum discord with increasing temperature for various drives, and specifically show the entanglement-to-discord transition curve for the time-modulated parametric drive.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares four different driving schemes (Parametric, Coherent, Modulated, Time-modulated Parametric) by analyzing the steady-state values of discord and entanglement as a function of temperature and coupling parameters.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems, as it models how engineered dissipation and driving fields can be used to control the transition between different types of quantum correlations (entanglement to discord) in cavity QED setups.
